source.title: CrossSplit: Mitigating Label Noise Memorization through Data Splitting
source.authors: Jihye Kim; A. Baratin; Yan Zhang; Simon Lacoste-Julien

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops CrossSplit to mitigate noisy-label memorization and reports its performance; it does not test the claim's original training setup.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 directly measures training accuracy on clean and noisy CIFAR samples. Other reported accuracy comparisons are test accuracy for the proposed method and baselines, not tests of the claim versions. No version-specific verdicts are assigned because results are for CrossSplit, a modified training procedure.
record.test_reason: The study uses noisy-label memorization to motivate CrossSplit and directly compares its strength with UNICON. These comparisons test a mitigation procedure, but establish neither complete random-label fitting, perfect training fit across corruption levels, nor real-label learning preceding noise memorization. A changed training procedure alone would not justify excluding a study; the reported outcomes do not establish any version here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that CrossSplit reduces noisy-label memorization and improves robustness on several image benchmarks. Maintaining clean-sample fit needs qualification at 90% noise; performance gains are also not universal, with weaker results on Tiny-ImageNet at 50% noise and CIFAR-10 above 92% noise.
record.recipe_differences: CrossSplit changes training by splitting labeled data between two networks, correcting labels with peer predictions, and using cross-split semi-supervised training.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, noise type and noise ratio affect results; the paper reports lower clean-sample training accuracy than UNICON at 90% noise, while test performance is higher.

fits_no_version.finding: CrossSplit has lower noisy-label training accuracy than UNICON and generally comparable clean-sample accuracy. At 90% noise, clean-sample accuracy is lower while test performance is higher.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-split training and peer label correction can reduce noisy-label memorization while preserving useful learning.

fits_no_version.finding: During supervised warm-up, noisy-label accuracy increases, especially on CIFAR-100. After warm-up, noisy-label accuracy often falls; it subsequently rises again for UNICON while CrossSplit continues suppressing memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy-label memorization dynamics depend on the transition from supervised warm-up to the subsequent robust training procedure.

record.code_released: https://github.com/nazmul-karim170/UNICON-Noisy-Label (UNICON baseline code rerun; CrossSplit code URL not stated)
record.problems: The memorization comparisons in Figure 2 are figure-only with no stated numerical values or uncertainty. Experiments cover simulated noisy labels at selected noise settings, not complete random relabeling or the original claim's unchanged training setup.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direct clean/noisy training-accuracy conditions reported beyond the Figure 2 settings were omitted. Test-accuracy benchmark tables and ablations concern CrossSplit performance rather than the specific claim versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test performance on completely random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown as corruption increases. CrossSplit versus UNICON test-accuracy trajectories do not supply this comparison.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep and steadily increasing test error toward chance. The benchmark test-accuracy sweep does not establish the joint claim.
Necessity and sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation for random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Shared real-data patterns being learned before noisy labels. Section 4.5 reports increasing noise memorization during warm-up and subsequent mitigation, without establishing the claimed ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains Figure 2's caption and discussion but no readable plotted values. Its qualitative comparisons are supported; absolute accuracy levels and learning-order claims cannot be reconstructed. The benchmark tables largely import baseline results, so their CE entries are not independent tests by this study.

versions.untested_parts: Random labeling and fitting it under the original architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost relative to fitting true labels and convergence versus corruption fraction.
The claimed sweep from no corruption to all labels corrupted, perfect training fit throughout, and steadily rising test error for standard networks.
Whether explicit regularizers or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting or are needed for true-label generalization.
Whether real and completely random labels are learned differently over training.
